JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that, the deceased who died in an accident on 24.08.2018 at about 7.15 p.m, involving the BBMP Compactor lorry vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AG-1209 which belongs to respondent No.1.

The deceased was running a Body building garage, the offending vehicle was taken to a garage of deceased for some repair, the offending vehicle was BBMP Compactor dumping truck used for collection and disposing of Garbage, when the deceased was dealing with the repair, the driver of truck due to his negligent act has wrongly operated the hydraulic leaver system and on account of which, the entire tail gate body of bucket has collapsed on the body of the truck, the deceased was dealing with his work could not able to foresee this mishap was hit by a portion of the said bucket, on account of which deceased sustained severe injuries to head and died on the spot.
The accident in issue had occurred due to negligent handling of the offending vehicle driver.
Soon after the accident the deceased body was shifted to Ambedkar Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein Postmortem was conducted and the corpse was handed over to the family members.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally and also lost their bread winner of the family.

Further the petitioners have spent substantial amount towards medical expenses,
transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
It is submitted that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, he was running body building garage and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.

The Jurisdictional Bagalur Police have registered a case UDR No.21/2018 for involving of BBMP Compactor Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01- AG-1209 and wrong handling the said Fareena Banu vs K.M. Manjunath on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140867080/
2 vehicle by its driver.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending BBMP Compactor Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AG- 1209.

The accident was occurred due to wrong handling of the driver of the offending BBMP Compactor Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AG-1209 and as such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Contending the above facts, they pray to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.

This respondent contended that in order to wangle the unlawful gain, the petitioners have suppressing the true facts have filed a false petition against this respondent and further she has not approached the court with clean hands to get compensation.
It is stated that initially after the accident the petitioner has given statement before the police as the incident occurred by an accidentally and her husband only responsible.
Further to get compensation she falsely submitting in this petition that the accident occurred by negligence of driver of Garbage Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AG-1209.
The charge sheet is also filed against the deceased and there is no mentioned anywhere that the accident was done due to the fault of the driver but after two years she filed this false petition.

It is stated that the deceased was negligently conducting the repair work of Garbage lorry without taking any precautionary safety methods, he was only one working amount with very heavy objects that were very dangerous to human life without taking minimum care, hence it discloses that the incident happen and occurrence of death due to his own negligence.
Further it is stated that upon complaint, the police registered the UDR and investigated the same and filed final report against the deceased.

The incident taken place on 24.08.2018 but this petition is filed on 09.10.2020, hence there is inordinate delay of two years that itself vibrantly discloses that the case is foisted so as to wangle the compensation amount from the respondents.
The respondent No.1 admitted that he is the RC owner of the Garbage Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AG-1209 and was duly insured with the 2nd respondent and same was in force as on the date of accident.
It is further submitted that at the time of incident the driver of the said vehicle also possess valid and effective driving licence and the said vehicle also possessing requisite licence.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. The respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement and additional written statement by contending that the petition is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01- AG-1209.

However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms &
conditions of the policy.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased as he was negligently conducting the repair work without taking the suitable precautionary measures.
Due to his own negligence the garbage bucket fell on him and the deceased was died.
At no point of time the driver was not at all in the driver seat at the material time of incident and except the deceased nobody was there in the said vehicle.
As such the question of negligence on the part of the driver does not arise at all.
The entire negligence is on the part of the deceased for his death.
Hence this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation or to indemnify the respondent No.1.

It is further stated that after the death of deceased the police have registered Fareena Banu vs K.M. Manjunath on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140867080/
3 the complaint under the UDR and after thorough investigation have submitted final report wherein the vehicle number of the respondent No.1 not at all mentioned.
This clearly goes to show that the involvement of the vehicle of the respondent is doubtful and hence this petition is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed.

Further this respondent stated that the entire facts, police records and the final reports clearly goes to show that the death is not due to any road traffic accident and it is absolutely a non RTA and on the other hand it is due to the self negligence of the deceased.

Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL and further the said vehicle did not holding valid and effective Permit and FC.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Non - compliance of section's 134(c), 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are only legal representatives of deceased 'Sri. Mohammed Dasthagar' and were dependent on him ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident that occurred on 24.08.2018 at about 7.15 p.m.,
at Body builder garage, Hosuru Bande village, Bidarahalli Hobali, Bengaluru East Taluk, Bengaluru City, due to the actionable negligence of the driver of HGV BBMP Compactor Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AG-1209 ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
6. Petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 9 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The petitioners have also examined the investigation officer as PW.2 and through him Ex.P.10 to 19 were got marked.
Further the petitioners have also examined the PSI-CCRB, Bengaluru as PW.3 and through him Ex.P.20 was got marked.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 has examined its Investigator as RW.1 and through her Ex.R.1 document was marked.
Further the respondent No.2 has also examined its Manager (Legal) as RW.2.
Further the respondent No.1 who is the owner of the offending vehicle got examined himself as RW.3.
Ex.R.2 to 8 were got marked through him.
The respondent No.1 has also examined the driver of the offending vehicle as RW.4.
Ex. R.9
was got marked through him.
7. Heard erudite counsel for the petitioners and respondents counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.2 : The petitioners have knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation on account of death of deceased in the incident occured at Garage on 24.08.2018 at about 7.15 p.m. It is the case of petitioners that, on 24.08.2018 when he was repairing the BBMP Compactor lorry vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AG-1209 its hydraulic bucket fell down on deceased who was mechanic.
For which he sustained serious head injuries and died at spot.
According to the petitioners at that time driver was present and operating the vehicle as per guidance of mechanic i.e., deceased.
It is relevant to note here that as per the documents there was no driver at the time of repair.
10. The respondents have contended that it is not coming under the RTA.
The incident took place during the repair of motor vehicle and was self negligence of the deceased.
Therefore, the respondents have not liable to pay any compensation.
11. The petitioners examined the the petitioner No.1 as PW.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 9.
As per Ex.P.1 initially it was filed as a UDR No.21/2018 of Bagalur Police.
Thereafter the petitioner No.1 lodged complaint then it was converted as FIR.
Admittedly, as per Ex.P.4 death of Mohammed Dastagir caused due to the head injury.
As per the police records, there was no involvement of driver and even the system or engine is/ was off there is a possibility of fell the hydraulic bucket.

In this regard the IO has issued requisition to the RTO as per Ex.P.17 and got answers to the questions which reads as under :

-      On careful perusal of the above Ex.P.17, it clears that even without operating the lever tail gate (bucket) it is possible to fell down.
The petitioner examined the IO as PW.2 in his chief-examination he clearly stated the driver was not present at the time of repair.
The advocate for petitioner with permission of the court treated the witness as hostile witness and cross examined at length but nothing was elicited in his mouth in favour of petitioners.
The petitioners have also examined the another IO as PW.3.
the PW.3 deposed by narrating the manner of conducting investigation.
The advocate for petitioner with permission of the court treated the witness as hostile and cross examined at length but nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.3 in favour of petitioners.
The petitioner No.1 is the complainant.
She could have challenged the final report.
But complainant / petitioner no.1 not challenged the said final report filed by the IO.

As per the documents produced by the petitioners,
the said incident was a accident but not coming under the Road Traffic Accident.

sentences.text: the RW.1 in his chief-examination deposed that, deceased was negligently conducting the repair work without taking any suitable precautionary measures.
Due to his own negligence the garbage bucket fell on his and deceased was died.
No point of time the driver was not at all in the driver seat at the material time of incident and except the deceased no person was their.
Therefore the question of negligence on the part of the driver does not arise.
Therefore the police have registered the UDR and investigated the same and submitted the report accordingly.
She has produced investigation report which is marked as Ex.R.1.
It reveals that the said insurance company investigated through their investigator as per Ex.R.1 as per the said report the driver was not present at the time of incident.
The respondents also examined its Manager by name Ashwini. J. as RW.2.
She deposed for with the contents of their written statement.
The respondent No.1 examined himself as RW.3.

In his chief- examination he deposed that the deceased was negligently conducting the repair work of garbage lorry without taking any precautionary safety measures and he was alone working with a heavy objects.
That were very dangerous to human life without taking minimum care.
The driver was not presented and vehicle was not moving and on.
Therefore, the question of negligence of driver does not arise.
He has produced RC copy, goods permit and FC, insurance policy etc.,
The respondents have also examined the driver of the said lorry as RW.4.
He deposed that he left the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AG-1209 for repair at garage of deceased on 22.08.2018 at 1.00 p.m and he had gone to lunch.
After lunch, he had not return to the garage because deceased told him that he would returned the vehicle after two days.

Thereafter his vehicle Fareena Banu vs K.M. Manjunath on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140867080/
6 owner told him about the incident.
In the cross-examination he admitted that to operate the hydraulic system the engine must be on condition.
13. The evidence of the petitioner and respondents clearly reveals that, the driver was not present during the incident and even engine was off mode, the hydraulic gazette fell down.
The Ex.P.17 clearly reveals that, to operate the hydraulic system i.e., to lift up the bucket or gazette the engine must be on mode.

But even in the off condition there is possibility of come down the gazette /
bucket.
It is issued by the Assistant RTO who is the expert in the mechanical engineering.
The report can be considered and as such it clears that incident took place due to the self negligence of deceased and it is not coming under the Road Traffic Accident.
The accident took place at garage.
It is not a public place.
Therefore it is not coming under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.
14. It could be culled out from this that, it is a case of self-negligence of the deceased himself while he was repair the vehicle.
The petitioners are not entitled for any compensation as the petitioners have failed to prove the accident happened because of rash and negligent driver of the alleged vehicle.
The evidence placed on record discloses that, at the time of repair the vehicle driver was not present and vehicle was in off mode.
It was occurred in between the four wall.
Further a critical evaluation of the entire material available on record, proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accident occurred purely on account of fault of the deceased.
Hence this Tribunal answers issue No.2 In the Negative.
15. ISSUES NO.1, 3 & 4 : In view of the discussion made supra, issues No.1 & 3 do not survive for consideration.

Consequently, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby dismissed with costs.
Draw an award accordingly.
